name: Holi
description: Festival of colours marking the triumph of Holika's burning and arrival of spring. Most vibrant in Mathura & Vrindavan.

name: Diwali
description: Festival of Lights celebrating Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya. Celebrated with oil lamps, fireworks, and sweets.

name: Durga Puja
description: Kolkata's grand festival honouring Goddess Durga with elaborate themed pandals and cultural events over 5 days.

name: Onam
description: Kerala's harvest festival celebrating King Mahabali's annual return. Features the 26-course Sadya and Vallam Kali snake boat races.

name: Pongal
description: Tamil harvest festival thanking the sun, rain, and farm animals. Rice cooked outdoors and allowed to boil over as a symbol of abundance.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: Mumbai's grandest festival — clay Ganesh idols installed for 10 days, then immersed in the sea. Lokmanya Tilak made it a public festival in 1893.

name: Pushkar Camel Fair
description: World's largest camel fair in Pushkar — 50,000+ camels traded alongside cultural performances, folk music, and the sacred Pushkar Lake.

name: Baisakhi
description: Sikh New Year and harvest festival marking the founding of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699. Grand celebrations at the Golden Temple.

name: Bihu
description: Assam's harvest festival celebrated three times a year. Rongali Bihu (April) is the biggest, featuring Bihu dance in traditional gamosa and mekhela chador.

name: Navratri / Garba
description: Nine nights of Garba and Dandiya-Raas dance circles honoring Goddess Durga. Gujarat's Navratri holds the Guinness record for world's largest dance.

name: Hemis Festival
description: The largest annual festival of Ladakh at Hemis Monastery — features masked Cham dances and display of a giant Thangka painting every 12 years.

name: Kumbh Mela
description: The world's largest human gathering — pilgrims bathe at the confluence of sacred rivers. Held at Haridwar, Prayagraj, Nashik, and Ujjain in rotation.
